utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. Case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet everyone in the courtroom. I believe that Mr. Karnavas needs another seven minutes which means that he will have had 90 minutes in total. Mr. Karnavas, you have seven minutes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I'll try to do it in less. I want to show you a document, sir, and I'll read it for you because we don't have the B/C/S version. But if I can put it on the ELMO. And for the record, it's 1D 01048. This is a document from ECMM. It's dated 17 October, 1993. Now, before I pose the question to you, I just want to recap. Yesterday we talked a little bit about Cibo and his functions. Do you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you recall us agreeing that Cibo was appointed by Izetbegovic to be in charge of three municipalities, Jablanica, Konjic and Prozor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, here these are some minutes of a meeting it appears. And I'm going to need Madam Usher to actually turn the second page because I want to read a passage from it. This would be with respect to Mr. Cibo. This is -- we'll be revisiting this document, Your Honours, at some other point, so I don't want to go into the entire contents, but this was a meeting where my client, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, attended along with Mate Granic, the then Foreign Minister of the Republic of Croatia. You will see that it was a very constructive meeting. And then it goes on on page 2 that there apparently had a meeting with Mr. Cibo, and I'm going to read slowly what Mr. Cibo's position was and then pose a question to you. Mr. Cibo stated that if -- well, I first have to go back up, I guess. "MI," that would be Mostar 1, "has met today Mr. Cibo Safet, president of the War Presidency in Jablanica. He stressed that there could be no possible political solution in this conflict without: "1. Punishment of the aggressors who, according to him were the Croats. He said here that in the eyes of the world community, Croatia is not acclaimed as an aggressor country, and that this is one of the reasons why the solution of this whole conflict is not getting anywhere. "2. Negotiations between Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and all the legitimate leaders of the nations of the world, Mr. Tudjman, Mr. Milosevic, Lord Owen and Mr. Stoltenberg are not legitimate leaders of any state and therefore they are not able to negotiate about the future presence of Bosnia. Nor is the UN for the same reasons. "3. Realising the fact that no new state could be based on ethnic principle." Mr. Cibo goes on to say: "Mr. Cibo stated that if these requirements could not be met, the Muslims would be willing to fight until there was no single Muslim left in the area of former Yugoslavia. He also said the Muslims were against ethnic cleansing. He added that everybody would have to accept the fact that there would never be a Greater Serbia, a Greater Croatia, nor a Muslim State. As a consequence of this, people by the next count of population would simply be listed as Bosnians and not as Muslims, Croats, et cetera." This was Mr. Cibo's stated position. Apparently, one would think that this is also Mr. Alija Izetbegovic's position since that he was more or less his Viceroy in that region back in 17 October, 1993. Sir, would it not appear that Mr. Cibo is advocating a policy wherein there would be no nations recognised, no constituent nations recognised in Bosnia-Herzegovina as was recognised by the then existing constitution?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an extract from a text that I don't have in the B/C/S. It's an extract, but I'm not familiar with the context. Cibo knew that the statements weren't always appropriate, but I wouldn't agree with you that he literally represented what Alija Izetbegovic was fighting for. I don't believe that these are Alija Izetbegovic's positions. As far as I am aware, given the extent of my contact with Alija Izetbegovic, he was always for avoiding a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats. That was his position. And he always asked us and beseeched us not to do anything that would pose a threat to the relationship between the Muslims and the Croats. Why did they send Cibo into this area? Well, since we're short of time, I can't go into all the details. There was only some things we found out about after the war. There were some documents that surfaced about how he arrived there. He was sent to the area of Jablanica and Konjic because there was a parallel power structure in Jablanica apparently and that was unacceptable because they thought that that meant we had accepted HVO authority. However, there were rumours and -- according to which the head of the municipality of Konjic, I can't remember his name, had already accepted the structure in Konjic, the HVO structure in Konjic. That's why Cibo had apparently been sent down there. But to be quite objective, I don't think we needed him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Cibo was an extremist, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's difficult to describe him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of his statements, even the text you've just read out, point to the fact that he was an extremist and other statements don't seem to be the statements of an extremist, but it was difficult to cooperate with him. He replaced all of us as soon as he arrived down there. He gathered some people around him, and we knew that they weren't the sort of people they should have been. When he arrived there, our situation became far more complex because local people could no longer officially control the situation in Jablanica. At the time, we lost control of many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I expect that you will later accuse me and some of my colleagues of having done certain things up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That at the time we didn't have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Undoubtedly Alija Izetbegovic knew exactly what Cibo was up to though, didn't he, because he was being informed of Cibo's activities? And I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have the next Defence team, please. Ms. Alaburic, how much time do you have at your disposal? If we do the calculations --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I have an hour and a half. That's the amount of time you granted me. And I also have the time given to me by my colleague Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and I hope that I'll have sufficient time to cover at least some of the subjects with Mr. Idrizovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Idrizovic. My name is Ms. Alaburic. I'm a lawyer from Zagreb. I represent Mr. Petkovic. I won't be accusing you of anything, but I believe that as you have done so far, you will assist us in understanding certain things a little better. I'll take up from where Mr. Karnavas stopped. He was talking about Mr. Cibo. And please have a look at a document in my bundle of documents. 4D 00452. It's an order from Sefer Halilovic. 00 -- 4D 00452. Mr. Idrizovic, it might be simpler to just look at the screen so as not to waste time with the documents. This is an order from Mr. Sefer Halilovic in which Safet Cibo is being assigned to the Mostar 4th Corps. Please have a look at the following document now, 4D 00450. While waiting for it to appear on the screen, I'll tell you what this will document is. It's a letter from the SDA regional committee in Herzegovina, and it says at the meeting of the central and executive -- and part of the Executive Board of the SDA, it was concluded that Mr. Safet Cibo should be assigned to the regional committee of Herzegovina as a full member. Mr. Karnavas asked you about appointing Mr. Cibo as the president of three municipalities, and now we have a document that concerns the army and the SDA political party. These documents on the basis of which Mr. Cibo had power in party and in the army and within the civilian bodies.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can remember, I answered this question yesterday although no one asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. So those are the three documents concerned. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by Mr. Karnavas, you said that Mr. Cibo was a little difficult, that sometimes his positions or the positions he expressed weren't the policies followed by Alija Izetbegovic. Yesterday, you also said that you didn't really get on with him, and you said that in the area of Jablanica and Konjic, someone else appeared with Mr. Cibo or, rather, some other military formations arrived with Mr. Cibo. Who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time in Jablanica or somewhat later, it's not really important when, first part of a unit came and then the entire unit came from Igman in Sarajevo. The name was the special unit -- unit for special purposes of the Supreme Command Staff. It was called Zuka's unit or Zulfikar Alispago, known as Zuka, was its commander. Part of it first arrived and then the entire unit came then. The silver fox unit came. It consisted of 10 or 15 men, and then the Igman or Igman Wolves or Cedo's Wolves also arrived. It was also a small unit from Igman. I can't really little tell you what their status was. As far as we were concerned, the status was non-existent, but I don't think those units were under the effective control of the corps when they arrived there and later on to avoid being asked other questions. The detachment for special purposes within the Supreme Command Staff shows who should have been in charge of it. The corps commander, the commander of the 4th Corps and later the 6th Corps, well, the name shows that it wasn't part of the corps. As to which formation it was a part of, I don't know. Don't ask me. Then I could speculate that this isn't the right place to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's draw a conclusion. Certain military units arrived, and you are telling us that they weren't part of the regular system of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were directly linked to the Main Staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I won't ask you who was in charge or in command of those units, but I'm interested in the following: What were the consequences of the arrival of those units in the territory around Jablanica and Konjic? You said that Cibo arrived and that units arrived and that corps's dissatisfaction among the Croats and the Muslims. How di the Croats feel? Do you know how they reacted, how the Croats reacted to the arrival of those units in your area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no one felt good about it, not just the Croats. I don't know how to put this. These people were young people. These men were young men. They were well-armed, and they were -- they had Ray-Bans. They were all arrogant. They'd been well fitted out. That's how it was. Don't laugh. In one village, well, they wreaked havoc because they married 20 young girls. The behaviour of General Daidza was similar. So these men were -- well, that's how they were. I don't know how to describe it. They weren't part of the structure or they weren't under effective control of anyone else. Whether there was someone who wanted things to function in this way, I don't know. All I can say is how things worked in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, when those units arrived did the relationship between the Croats and the Muslims deteriorate or improve or, rather, the relationship between the HVO and the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the whole, the situation deteriorated throughout that period, from April 1992 up until April 1993. The relationship continued to deteriorate during that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, that's quite enough. Let's move on to another question. Yesterday, in answer to a question from the Prosecution, you said that in May and June, 1992, the Croats took all the major hills in the southern and western part of the municipality of Jablanica, and you said almost literally, that at that point the ABiH army had been established or had the BiH army been established by then or had you been in a position -- rather, you said you had the ABiH army. You could have expelled them from those positions but you weren't allowed to do so by the leadership. Do you remember doing that -- saying that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Cibo arrived in the area of Jablanica and Konjic, was the difficulty of removing the HVO from those hills removed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When he arrived, the situation didn't change. I'm talking about the hills taken by the HVO in 1992 or, rather, the elevations. They weren't affected up until the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you said that nothing changed. But in what sense did something change?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't understood you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said that in that sense the relationship to the HVO didn't change when Cibo arrived, but I believe that you wanted to say that in a certain sense the relationship did change. So I want to know whether I've understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you what that was all about if you want me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try. Until his arrival, our contacts with the HVO -- we had contacts with the HVO. There were never any problems especially when Marko Zelenika and I were there. There were really no problems and there weren't any problems later on. We still maintained contact. But with his arrival, our contacts ceased, not because we wanted them to cease, but because he wanted to be the individual who would be the liaison officer or contact with them. So that is why I said at the beginning that we weren't able to exercise effective control of the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, in answer Mr. Mr. Karnavas's question about the statement by Mr. Cibo, about some sort of Bosnian unitarianism, if I can simplify matters, this seemed to remind me of an answer you said -- gave yesterday, to the effect that in December, 1992, you talked to the president, Alija Izetbegovic, and asked him to answer questions about cantonisation. And from the way in which you spoke about this, I understood it that the BH army, on the territory of Jablanica, that is to say in your own units, was in fact opposed to the cantonisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina which would be based on the national criteria or ethnic criteria. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you didn't. We always said we're going to respect any decision that the authorities take, that the authorities agree upon. Now, since this was not agreed upon, cantonisation was the subject of discussion, but it was not a fait accompli. It was not something that was decided upon. Then we said, let politics do its work and once they reach an agreement when -- we'll follow suit. We're not going to do anything against that. We just wanted to have these agreements rounded off and agreements actually reached. And the problem here was that the local representatives of the HVO used this subject of discussion as something that had already been agreed upon. So the cantonisation of Bosnia on ethnic grounds was being discussed. Herzegovina belonged to the Croats and they wanted to put it into effect. Now, we were opposed to this until an actual agreement had been reached.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, that's another subject again. Just slow down a bit. And in this sense, we're interested in whether the BH army really did implement this policy, but with regard to the military operations or did individuals in the BH army have some of their own political goals? And I'll remind you, in this regard, of a document that was presented by the Prosecutor. It is P 00614, and it is the records from a meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Jablanica held on -- or, rather, held in December, 1992, and it was literally stated in point 2 of that document of the records, relating to the political and security situation, that in Jablanica, in the fifth section this is, and I'm going to quote: "We should state loud and clear that the three ethnic groups, entities, which are being imposed now, will not be accepted by the Muslim people."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got anything on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I gave the wrong number. It should be P 00624. 624 is the correct number. And it is, as I said, the minutes of the session of the Municipal Assembly dated the 22nd of October, 1992, and point 2 was devoted to the political and security situation in Jablanica municipality. The Staff Commander of the armed forces of Jablanica at that time, and this is in section 5, said that "we should state loud and clear that the three ethnic communities will not be accepted by the Muslim people, and an attempt to implement this, at all cost, would lead to a civil war." Those words are very similar to what my colleague Mr. Karnavas said when quoting Mr. Cibo, contained in the document of the European Monitors, observers. Now, tell me, do you have any knowledge about this? Did you know that many some of the representatives of the ABiH army would be opposed to this internal division which would be based on national or ethnic grounds?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I only have the beginning of this document. I can't see the portion you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: For us, too, it is not clear where the passage is to be found because it's a rather voluminous document. If you could indicate more precisely that would be very kind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it was point 2 of the minutes, the fifth section. In the B/C/S text, it is on page 5. But I quoted the passage, so I don't think there's any need for us to spend time on that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My question is as follows: There were individuals in the BH army who were opposed to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise to counsel, but I must say I'm with Judge Trechsel on this. I'd like to see. When the language is being put to the witness, I would like to be able to see the particular language and the context of it. If we could please be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I -- as I said, it is part of the minutes relating to point 2. In the minutes, it says exactly what point 2 is about, and it is the fifth section. We have it on our screens, and it begins with the following words, "Ako, if". And what I quoted was the last part of that portion. "It should be stated large and clear that the three ethnic groups are being imposed now will not be accepted by the Muslim people and attempts to implement it at all costs would lead to a civil war."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or words to that effect because the interpreters don't have it in English on their screens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That has been extracted from the context. Read out the previous passage where it says "Units of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have read everything, Mr. Idrizovic. Tell me, did you read the book by Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether that -- from that book it emerges that Mr. Sefer Halilovic was without a doubt opposed to the internal division of Bosnia-Herzegovina which would be based on the national principle or ethnic principle?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You agree?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked to slow down for the benefit of the interpreters and the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that he was not the only member of the BH army who held political views of that kind?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that while Sefer Halilovic was in command of the army, that within its composition, there were 25 per cent of non-Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the political --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I waited for the translation. The interpreter is asking you please kindly slow down, and I only interpret their words and request. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, my question was as follows: Can you agree with the position taken that Sefer Halilovic was not the only member of the BH army who was opposed to the internal division of Bosnia-Herzegovina based on the national criteria?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He couldn't have been alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us whether you ever heard -- can you agree with me when I say that the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina could be interpreted as a civil war because of the different views people had on the internal set-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there's some people here --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Just give me a yes or no answer?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to give a yes or no answer to that question. I think it is a religious war as well, that it was an aggression, that it is a civil war, and there is no category of war that you could not apply to this particular war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I'd now like, Mr. Idrizovic, for us to take a look at the documents of the BH army which relate to the conflicts. I'm not going to begin with April, 1993, but with March, 1993. So would you now please take a look. And in my set of documents, if you can find the document, if not, we can focus on our screens. The document is 4D 00438.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say, 4 --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is a document which is not very legible, and that's what it says in the translation as well, but those who know the names of the units, who are familiar with the names of the units, will be able to see that it -- we're talking about 7th brigade, the Suad Alic Brigade from Konjic, and a letter from the commander, Midhat Cerovac. It is dated the 23rd of March, 1993, in which it says the following: "We inform the 4th Corps that the situation in the area of responsibility is as follows: 150 members of the HVO captured, the town blocked, life in the town paralysed. We continue with the arrests." Tell us, please, Mr. Idrizovic, perhaps we could just remind the Court of your words when you said that the situation in Jablanica could not be understood or followed unless we know about the events that took place in a broader area, including the neighbouring municipalities of Jablanica and Mostar and Konja. I meant to say Konjic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, do you know about these events in Konjic? Were you familiar with them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know about those events, and I think I said yesterday or previously that all of us -- or what I want to say is this: All those who say that they knew what was going on within the encirclement are not telling the truth. We are under -- we were under such a siege. We were under such a blockade and taken up with our own affairs that if we're going to tell the truth as human beings then, objectively speaking, we didn't know what was going on there. And I'm under oath here. I took the solemn declaration. And I claim that I never knew that on the 23rd -- is that what it says, the 23rd of March, yes -- that 150 members of the HVO were captured. I really didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Let's move on to the next document 4D 00081. And it is a document from Mr. Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say 4D --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D 00081. It is a document from Mr. Arif Pasalic dated the 7th of April, 1993, and it is addressed to the Municipal Staff for the defence of Jablanica. You can see that in the lower portion. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in that order, among other things, the following is stated: "Undertake all necessary measures and steps in the spirit of our previous order to place the units under full combat readiness as was ordered." Can you see that order and point 1 of it? Can you explain to us, what was the previous order to place units under full combat alert?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the previous order was. I assume you have that previous order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember what that previous order was so that you could tell us what time it was issued?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't want to speculate once again. I'm sure that you have the order. You ought to have it because you found it like all the other ones. It is the archives of the 4th Corps seized by the HVO in May, 1993, the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not interested in hearing your explanations.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to speculate. I don't want to say what this order or the previous order was because it's been 15 years since that time after all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us point 6 of the order? It says: "Protect the secrecy of our own activities and pay due attention." Does that mean planning some offensive activities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us the call for combat -- or, rather, the slogan at the end: "For a free Bosnia-Herzegovina until final victory." That slogan that is in capital letters at the end of the text. Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really can't. Everybody wrote something at the end. That comes under morale boosting and propaganda and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next document then. Let's move on to the next document and the number is 4D 00082. It is also an order from Arif Pasalic dated the 14th of April, 1993, addressed to the Municipal Staff of Jablanica among others. Is that right, Mr. Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what this order is about? "You must not allow members of the Spanish Battalion to leave Jablanica." What's all that about? What was that about? And why did Mr. Arif Pasalic issue an order to that effect, not to allow UNPROFOR to leave Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why? Well, I can't speak in his name and say why. The Spanish Battalion was put up in the town of Jablanica. It was deployed in a stadium on -- in an open space and there were rumours going round at that time, and we're talking about the 14th of April because the conflicts in the Neretvica river valley had already begun. In Doljani and Sovici, the situation had reached a head and we, together with the representatives of the Spanish battalion and the European Monitors, toured the area to see what was happening and war was looming in the air. Yes, I'll get to that. Just a moment. I'll get to that. I'm speaks as slowly as possible for the people to be able to interpret properly and to be recorded properly. It was expected that if the Spanish Battalion or, rather, if the HVO attacks Jablanica, the Spanish Battalion would try to pull out, because faced with a situation of that kind, it could have been the victim, too. And this actually happened at a certain point in time later on. A shell actually did hit them and two members of the Spanish Battalion were killed. So the intention was to have the Spanish Battalion stay there to be a witness and if the HVO were to attack us, let them be in the target area, too. Probably, that was it. I'm saying this. I'm giving you my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. So the answer, in fact, if I've understood you correctly, is that you do not know what Mr. Arif Pasalic wanted to achieve by issuing that order and why he gave the order.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know but that that was what I assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, 4D 00453. This is a letter from the HVO Brigade commander in Konjic, Mr. Zdravko Sagolj. It's very brief. We can read through it. "Konjic was attacked by forces that arrived from Bradina and Igman. We are doing all we can to neutralise their action. They are exerting much pressure from Jablanica on the area of Klis. We shall attempt to do something in Jablanica, too, in order to engage those forces (they have surrounded our forces in Doljani and Sovici) but we can't do anything effectively ourselves alone. Start acting in accordance with the prior agreement immediately. Zlatar and Boksevica have been surrounded and cannot maintain their position. Hurry up. Inform Prozor. They say they can't help us at all. They say they have no orders. In Konjic, Celebici, and Radesine, up there, you should assess. Including Kiseljak in the sector of Ivan Planina, engage forces with the artillery in Prozor [as interpreted] until something is done concretely. Start moving while we're still alive." Mr. Idrizovic, were you familiar with the position in Prozor as described in this letter?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was on the 15th of April. Jablanica had already been attacked. We were dealing with our own problems. I can't say what was happening in Konjic. Konjic had been cut off for three or four days. We didn't have any contact with Konjic, any communication with Konjic. What Mr. Sagolj has written confirms what I have already said here yesterday or the day before yesterday. Everyone was dealing with their own problems. No one could help anyone. You can see that Mr. Sagolj is asking for assistance. Nobody was sending him any assistance. That was our situation. That was everyone's situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I'd just like to correct something in the transcript on page 19, line 19. Instead of the word "Prozor" it should say "Konjic", since the letter I read concerns the area of Konjic. Let's move on. Everyone was dealing with their own problems. Mr. Idrizovic, if the HVO was planning to launch an attack in the direction of Jablanica, and that would include the immediately neighbouring municipality of Konjic, would it be possible that on the same day the HVO in Konjic would prepare such a letter and you would draw a conclusion on the basis of the letter that everyone was trying to save what they had in the area under their control. Could you explain that very briefly though?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't quite understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, you said that everyone was dealing with their own problems. This can be seen in this letter and that includes HVO units. They were dealing with their own problems.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So it don't show that there was planned action and a joint action hadn't been planned by all those forces. You can't say that.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said on a local level, people were dealing with their own problems. Please don't ask me what happened -- about what happened in Konjic. I really don't know nor could I have known. And no one from Jablanica could have known what was happening in Konjic and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, we've now opened up two subjects. Let's try and first deal with the subject I'm trying to clarify by putting these questions to you and it concerns this statement of yours. If you yourself have come to the conclusion that individual HVO units were exclusively concerned with what was happening in their area, in their territory, and if these things were happening on the 15th of April, the only logical conclusion is that on the 15th of April, there was no planned HVO attack in the area of Jablanica and Konjic. Would you agree with that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. All I said is that the situation was such that we, at the local level, dealt just with our own problems. As to what someone planned at a higher level, well, I know nothing about that. But from Mr. Sagolj's letter -- on the basis of Mr. Sagolj's letter, you can prove what I'm saying, that we were all dealing with our own problems and that includes Mr. Sagolj.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's just what I wanted to show. Thank you for that answer because I think it reflects the actual situation on the ground. With regard to your answers that relate to not knowing anything about the situation in Konjic, well, since you're a witness who is supposed to explain to us the events in Jablanica and the surrounding places, I have to put the following question to you. Is it possible to understand the events in Jablanica and in the neighbouring places if you have no knowledge of what was happening in Konjic? Try and be objective in your answer.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've lived in Zagreb and you can't understand what I'm saying. People who went through the war can understand me. These gentlemen here know what it was like. You don't. We could only move around within a diameter of 10 kilometres, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, when I put my questions to you, I'm not assuming that you were able to move around freely and that you had certain knowledge. I'm asking you something simple. Is it possible to understand the events in Jablanica if one is unaware of what was going on in the neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. We couldn't know what was happening elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I'm not asking you whether you could have known anything about that. I understand you when you say that if you were involved in combat, et cetera, you were only familiar with the situation in your area. But my question is: Is it possible to understand the events in one place, for example, Jablanica, without trying to explain the events in the neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you look back at the situation now, then you can see that these events were linked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And that's why I want to show you and the Judges documents that also concern the neighbouring municipalities. This is an order to have a better understanding of the events in Jablanica, Sovici, and Doljani, and these places are referred to in the indictment. And this is why I would now like to have a look at the following document, 4D 000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you know that we rendered a decision in which we've said that the tu quoque defence was not acceptable. If you want the witness to say that the ABiH was guilty of committing atrocities, well, you can spend many hours doing this, but this doesn't mean that we will be taking this into account in the judgement. We're not judging the ABiH. We are judging the charges directed at some of the accused. The ABiH isn't on trial here. We're not dealing with what happened that Konjic. You can ask him whether he knows what happened in Konjic and he'll say yes or no, and the Judges will be intelligent enough to understand the answer. But don't spend minutes or hours on this subject, given that the witness doesn't want to play your game.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to answer that, and I have to respond to that objection. I don't think it's appropriate objection, because I'm not trying to point to crimes committed by the ABiH. My sole purpose was to clarify offensive and defensive action in mid-April, 1993. The reason for this is as follows: The question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's your objective, ask him whether the ABiH carried out an attack on the 14th of April, and I'll say yes or no, and you can continue in that way. Deal with the substance. The Defence keeps complaining about not having enough time. The Judges have noted that you're not dealing with the crux of the matter. You want to show that there were attacks or defensive action taken by the ABiH. You have a former member of the military here. Ask the witness whether the ABiH was involved in an attack in April. He'll say no, perhaps, and then you can show him a document that contradicts him, et cetera, et cetera. I'm not going to lecture you on how to proceed when conducting your cross-examination, that's not my role. My role is to avoid wasting time. When you use time intelligently, constructively, then we can only approve this. But when we notice that you are following a route that is not of much use, I must inform you of the fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I ask the witness a direct question about whether there was an ABiH attack in April, 1993, I'm quite certain that the witness would say no. And similarly, if I put the same sort of question to an HVO officer about HVO attacks, this witness -- or such an officer would also say no. So I believe that by putting such direct questions, I can't obtain an appropriate answer from the witness. I'm sorry if you believe that I'm wasting my time. I don't share that opinion, and I believe that in Jablanica and Sovici and Doljani certain facts have been accepted from the Tuta and Stela case. These are facts that we now have to refute at this stage, and these adjudicated facts also say that the HVO planned an attack on Jablanica and that the attack on Sovici and Doljani was part of the planned action. The events in Sovici and Doljani were part of a planned action to expel the population from that area, and my questions are being put to the witness in order to prove that there was combat in the wide area of Jablanica and Konjic, and these areas are linked up. Conflicts would spill over from one area into the other. And I'm trying to show that certain military activities had been planned or, rather, certain HVO military activities had, as the purpose, the achievement of certain objectives, and this was the result of ABiH action. So things aren't quite simple when we are talking about who was attacking and who was defending themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not a soldier, but perhaps General Petkovic could have put a question to the witness as a soldier. You know that when there's a military action, there are orders. There are preparatory orders, there are orders that concern reports on actions. There are debriefings. That's how things work in all armies throughout the world. If you're trying to show the ABiH was involved in a military operation, the witness in front of you would have been immediately aware of it. So use your questions and documents to go to the crux of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all I'm trying to say is the following: It's an indisputable fact that the ABiH had more territory under its control after the conflict with Croats than it had at the beginning. And I'm sure we won't find a single document from the ABiH in which we can see that an attack is being ordered. But now I'll ask my client, Mr. Petkovic, to provide an explanation for the reason for which such questions are being put.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we talked about the arrival of Safet Cibo and his arrival in the area of Konjic and Jablanica. Witness, on the 23rd -- on the 20th of March, did Safet Cibo become the chief of these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was appointed halfway through the month.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen documents of the commander of the brigade Suad Alic who launched an attack in the area of Konjic as ordered by the 4th Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not prior to today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Not before today. Sir, you were link to the 4th Corps, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen the report of Mr. Cerovac before today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you in contact with the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see in the document of the 23rd of March the stamp of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about this Cerovac documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Was the deputy commander of the 4th Corps, who was known as Tetak, in Jablanica at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the attack, yes, on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: So you know about that too?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You've been shown an order dated the 4th of April, I think. From the commander of the 4th Corps, it was also addressed to you. It was to raise the level of combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: It refers to an earlier order that you weren't familiar with?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was familiar with it. I didn't say I wasn't. All I said is that, at this point in time, I couldn't remember. You'd have to show it to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: That previous order, was it a link to the beginning of the conflict in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If you have the order, show it to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you have told us, you established a chronology of the events and I think that the orders of the 4th Corps are orders that you have included in your chronology of events. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: So now we have concluded that the link on raising the level of combat orders concerns an earlier order about launching an offensive in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there could be a link.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a serious question. I can't talk about something I don't have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's talk about the next order you were shown several days afterwards. It's again the 4th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you are talking about documents, perhaps you could provide the number so that we can see it on the screen, because the witness said that he couldn't see the document. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Could we have the first order from the corps? Date -- dated the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order dated the 7th of April, 4D 00081.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see that order of the 7th of April? It was shown to you previously.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I don't know what number you mean now. I'm looking for it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You have it on your screens.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You took a look at the first point of the order. "Undertake all necessary measures and actions in the spirit of our previous order on placing the units on full combat alert or full combat readiness as was ordered." Now if we're dealing with the 7th of April here, this document is the 7th of April, and on the 20th of March was the blockade and attack on Konjic and 150 members of the HVO captured and the next day the arrests and captures continue. You saw that document.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the logical link between that and this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You cannot say that. Now, the next document which my attorney showed you, was the next order to raise combat readiness and it is the 14th of April. That was the date.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: May I have a number, please, counsel, for that document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Bench and everybody else, it is 4D 00082. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take a look at the order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if we go back to the 23rd of March, and here we have the date as being the 14th of April, Arif Pasalic is still the commander of the 4th Corps, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: All the orders that we've seen are continuous orders following on from each other, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These orders, yes they are. They are orders from the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. So they all raise combat readiness in the area; is that right? There's no letting up?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the situation deteriorated from one day to the next.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me this. You mentioned or, rather, we mentioned the 23rd of March, the blockade of Konjic, the arrests that took place, 150 members on the first day and I don't know how many HVO soldiers on the second day. Now, do you know about Turje, Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, those places?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: How far are they from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's almost the suburb of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the international observers and everybody else who spent time in the area consider that to be a small Croatian enclave?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that in the broader area of the town of Konjic, it was only this small portion, this small area where the Croats and up to 150 Croatian soldiers remained in an area not controlled by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Petkovic, but don't ask me about Konjic, please, because the situation in Konjic was very -- well, I haven't got any information about that. So don't ask me about Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I just asked you something that you do know about. You have already told me that a man nicknamed Tetak came to Jablanica, and as far as I know, this man named Tetak was the deputy commander of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Sulejman Dudakovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, could my counsel show us the order by Arif Pasalic dated the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Arif Pasalic the 16th of -- it's 4D 00084. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see this order of the 16th of April? First of all, is it the command of the 4th Corps that issued this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it is. Yes. Yes, yes it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: And it says the addressees, the Municipal Staff of Jablanica, the command of that staff was who?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You, right. So you were within the command of the 4th Corps and every document thus far was addressed to you too?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if every document, but most of the -- but documents did arrive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: The documents I showed you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's read through this document. It says: "Pursuant to a piece of information from the supreme defence staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the situation among the HVO forces in the region of Neretvica is as follows: "1. They are faced with a difficult situation. They are in a difficult position because they do not have enough manpower. They demand that their artillery from Risovac attack our positions north of the Neretvica. The HVO informs that the ABiH forces have taken control of the village of Vile probably Vrce."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrce wasn't taken control of and Vile doesn't exist in the area. That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, anyway, that they are moving in the direction of Kostajnica and that they are ABiH forces. Point 3: "HVO units expect assistance in the form of reinforcements from Prozor from the north. And the HVO units in Kiseljak have been ordered to help them out and move through Bradina, via Bradina. The HVO from Neretvica will attempt to take control of the village of Grebivca."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Grebivca.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then we can't see the rest of the text. But what we can see at the bottom, it says "coordinate and unite."

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I can help you out, I have this order which is handwritten, and it is fully legible. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: We were referring to point 3. "HVO units accept reinforcement in manpower coming from Prozor, from the northern side, and HVO units in Kiseljak have been ordered to set out to assist them via Bradina." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: "The HVO from Neretvica will attempt to take control of the village of Grevici, because via Grevici, and Kucani, the infantry can move to assist them. That is an assumption. I hereby order, under 1, continue combat operations in your areas of responsibility and do not allow the arrival of new forces from the direction of Prozor. And I'd like to mention that it is Prozor, the village of Kucani and the village of Grebici as well as from the direction of Bradina." And number 2, "Dovetail and coordinate joint combat operations in order to carry out successful operations and in order to break down the forces of the HVO." Is that what it says in that point?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now 3: "This order must be acted upon immediately." And it says, "Send to the addressees." Tell me the brigade locations. The 43rd Brigade of the BH army, where was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: It was at Konjic. Where at Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was turned towards the Serb aggressor over there, towards the fighters of Bijelo and the Glavaticevo region mostly. I am not saying that it didn't act the other side too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many men held the front line towards the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long front line from Vrce, where the HVO held positions and where the Serb forces had their own positions and then via Konjic, Bijela, Borak, that area, and Gornja Neretva.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next brigade, the 44rd brigade of the army of BH.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Jablanica is it. So this order was sent to your brigade at Jablanica, that it should continue combat operations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now let's look at the 45th brigade. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neretvica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Neretvica. So that's Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entire Neretvica river valley, it is the right bank of Jablanica lake.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that that's the municipality. I just asked for specifications. Now to the military police, they are being included in this as well.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion of the military police was at the level of a corps, of corps strength, so it had three companies, one was in Mostar, one was in Jablanica and another one was in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Municipal Staff of Konjic was the next addressee. You were not at its head. And the Municipal Staff at Jablanica, you were at the head of the Municipal Staff?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: So on the 16th of April, sir, as the Municipal Staff of Jablanica and your own brigade as well, the 40, what did you say, the 44th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You received this order to dovetail your combat operations with the forces of two brigades in the area of Konjic municipality. Is that what it says in this order or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. I can't say it doesn't when that's what is written.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you know Konjic and the area around Konjic better than any of us here. Tell us, please, militarily speaking, how could the HVO bringing in reinforcements help Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be very difficult.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Very difficult. Now, if they wanted to assist, was it only Prozor-Jablanica, from those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prozor Kiseljak is what is mentioned in the order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the territory, the area that is more southerly, the area of Prozor. That means -- and the Jablanica municipality because it's Jablanica and Ostrozac; right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, the HVO Brigade, how many battalions did it have?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mijo Tomic was the third, that means three.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, two battalions in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: How many brigades did the BH army have in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two brigades at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Right, two brigades. And the forces brought in by Cibo, you mentioned that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were those forces as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, did the staff of the Supreme Command with Cibo, send these troops to the Konjic-Jablanica area, and with the arrival of Cibo, did combat operations start immediately against the HVO? My calculations say that they started three days after Cibo arrived in the Konjic-Jablanica area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. No combat operations started with the arrival of Cibo, but the general situation deteriorated. The general political situation deteriorated, if I can put it that way, but no combat operations started with his arrival.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Please, we just noted that on the territory of two municipalities making up where the population is 70 per cent Muslim, Konjic and Jablanica, the HVO has one brigade there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if that same area, the Konjic municipality and Jablanica, the BH army has three brigades?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in Jablanica itself, you told us that you had 2.500 soldiers. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the whole war. There were never that many concentrated at any one time, but through the brigade, through the BH army during the war, so many soldiers passed through it, but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say that the HVO had 300 people in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents will tell you the exact figures and the HVO information and report will tell you the exact figures and the deployment of the people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say that the HVO had 300 men? And in your written statement, it says that we imprisoned 100 in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'm following you. I didn't understand what you just said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the HVO had 300 soldiers in Jablanica. Now, in your written statement given to the investigators, you mention that in town, in the town of Jablanica, for preventive reasons, you incarcerated 100 people at the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that we imprisoned a hundred people? That's not true.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can read your statement once again.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, fine, but I never said that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Witness, I'm going to go back once again to the 23rd of March. And this Court and all of us here have to know that Safet Cibo arrived before that and not long afterwards, not long afterwards, the conflict broke out. Now, for you, those of you who were within the 4th Corps chain of command, you do not know that on the 23rd of March the town of Konjic was blocked? I'll repeat it again. The town of Konjic was blocked. Somebody paralysed life in the town. Somebody arrested and took prisoner 150 soldiers of the HVO, and somebody, the very next day, continued with these arrests. Tell me please, do you know about Musala?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about Celibici?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell this Court whether they were prisons held by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Celebici and Musala, as far as I know, at the beginning, were joint prisons, joint prisons of the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about these joint things. I'm asking you who those prisons belonged to. Who had control of those prisons?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, they were held by the HVO and the BH army together and, probably after that, just by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: My next question is this: You said that you could help Konjic. Konjic could be helped out only from the area of Prozor, if you wanted to help Konjic militarily, is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could help it out on all sides but it depends on the available forces. You could help Konjic from Fojnica as well and Kiseljak as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. That's fine. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If somebody has three brigades to send there, then they could do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Militarily speaking, I'm asking you, if the HVO wanted to and if it decided to, could it, from the Konjic area, engage in fighting with the BH army in order to help the HVO in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said yesterday -- just a moment, please, I'm going answer your question. The situation was such that at that point in time nobody could help anybody. Not even God could help us down there any more. The situation was that complicated that all of us fended for ourselves. We did what we could to help ourselves. That's why I asked you not to ask me anything about Konjic, because I don't know about that. And I took the solemn declaration to tell the truth here and that's what I'm going to do. I'm going to tell the truth. I know nothing about the situation in Konjic, just as I know nothing about the situation somewhere else. I heard stories going round, but I don't want to speculate. All I want to say is what I know. So I don't know anything about the situation in Konjic but I do know for sure that the -- in Konjic, the Konjic Croats, the HVO could not have helped them from any direction just as the BH army could not have helped us in Jablanica, and that was the situation reflected further afield in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Everybody to had to fend for themselves and look out for themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I have one question, one more question about Konjic. Is there any military logics in the following, for anybody with two battalions, and you've just said that nobody could help anybody from any side, would it be logical for them to enter into conflict fighting two brigades and against forces that were brought in by Safet Cibo? Would that be logical from a military aspect?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not logical, but let's be quite clear here. Safet Cibo didn't bring in any respectable forces, any large forces. It was 3 to 400 men or one battalion strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, General Petkovic asked you a question and it is an important one. So you must give us a clear answer. General Petkovic, through his sequence of questions, is asking you in military terms, the following: In that particular area, Jablanica-Konjic, the HVO had a brigade strong. Forces were numbered a brigade. Now, if the BH army -- ABiH had three brigades or, rather, it did have three brigades. In your particular town, you had 2.500 soldiers, whereas the HVO had approximately 300. So according to General Petkovic, and the Chamber will check that out, 100 were preventively incarcerated. Now, the question that you're being asked by General Petkovic and that I am relaying to you is this: How come with that ratio of forces, it would be possible for the HVO, numerically far lower than compared to the number of forces the BH had, could launch an attack? So what answer could you give in military terms to this -- to what General Petkovic is putting to you? How come that the HVO who had so many less -- far less soldiers, how could it have launched an attack against a far mightier ABiH army? So that is what General Petkovic is asking you with his sequence of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. Well, I'd first like to correct something. The 44th Brigade never had 2.500 men. All I said is that in the course of the war in Jablanica, and I was referring to the Municipal Staff, the brigade, and the MUP, through these bodies 2 -- 2.500 men passed through all of these bodies, but the brigade never had 2.500 men at one point in time, but the war lasted for four years and there were many men who passed through, who were killed, et cetera. We haven't got time to go into all the military details now, but I think that, naturally, the HVO couldn't have launched an attack where the Herceg Stjepan Brigade was located, but I believe their strategy was to wait and see. They were waiting for someone to come from the outside and they'd be there to assist on the inside. That's what happened in Jablanica when Sovici and Doljani were attacked. And later on, this happened when there was an attack launched from the direction of Prozor towards Slatina. And also, there was this attack in June on Boksevica, et cetera. So in order to describe these events to you, I'll tell you when the HVO withdrew from Jablanica, when it moved its command, its troops, its police. Most of the families of those who had gone to Doljani remained in Jablanica. They believed that they would return down there in two or three days' time and they would join up with their families again. If they hadn't believed that this would happen -- if they hadn't believe that this would happen, if they hadn't counted on assistance from the outside, they certainly wouldn't have left their families in town and gone to this village to shell this town. In fact, they shelled their own families. I think that was the HVO plan. I'm assuming that that was the case. As a soldier, that's what I would assume. But naturally, inside, they didn't have the possibility of launching any military activity, any attack. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: My counsel showed you a Sagolj document and it says that forces from Jablanica were attacking from Ostrozac in the direction of Kostajnica. Was a brigade from Jablanica included in the attack on Kostajnica and Falanovo Hill and other areas around Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A brigade from Jablanica and we're talking about the 15th and 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: And of the 13th too.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of April, the Jablanica-Konjic road was blocked and the Radesine sector, check-point was set up, and from the direction of the Falanovo Hill, the Falan Hill, if you remember that part, it's in the direction of Ostrozac, the road was kept under fire to block the road to Konjic. On the 15th and 16th, we were using all of our forces to establish lines in the direction of Doljani and Slatina. Unfortunately, we didn't have those positions at the time. You know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, you said that the HVO tried to do something against the Serbs, but that you threatened them, and since they were aware that they were in an inferior position, they gave up on that idea. Did you say that or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: It's in your statement you gave to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could someone show that to me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to that statement later. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a brief comment with your leave. When reading the order dated the 16th of April, I emphasised Prozor and Jablanica. We'll come across HVO activities in Prozor on the 17th of April, on the 18th of April, and on the 19th of April, during that period of time. (redacted), a Prosecution witness, will also talk about this and we have shown this witness documents that relate to places in the municipality of Prozor, and that's why I put a question to the witness. If the HVO had to assist its forces or wanted to assist its forces in Konjic, how could they have done so in military terms? They would have had to leave from Prozor and then drive back the armija in the first village and then in the second village and then reach Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Kostajnica is the nearest?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes or, rather, it's the largest Croatian village and that's where the brigade command was located later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: So that's the largest village. Witness, we have the documents and the order shows that your brigade from Jablanica carried out military activity in Kostajnica. That's in the Prozor municipality. Tell me, in military terms, in order to stop your brigade, would it have been logical to cut of your routes from -- between Konjic and Jablanica, from Slatina-Ostrozac, so that you couldn't send forces into the municipality of Konjic? I'm asking you whether it's logical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, General. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in military terms -- in military terms, would it be logical, would it be justified if one wanted to prevent action of the forces from Jablanica in the direction of Konjic, would it be logical to take over the area between Jablanica and Konjic, to cut off access to Konjic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say just yes or no. I'll answer your question but not like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether this is military logic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're claiming something you have no evidence for. The 44th Brigade from Jablanica never carried out military action in the direction of Konjic, and a minute ago, we concluded that in the Neretvica sector, if the whole -- the entire Herceg Stjepan brigade had been there in the Neretvica, well, there was the 45th Brigade of the ABiH in Neretvica. Why would they need assistance from Jablanica? There was no need. And as far as your previous question is concerned, whether in military terms it would be logical for someone from Prozor to go to Kostajnica, well, naturally. That's not logical and that's not possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Why is it not possible? I'm interested in that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have a break now because it's 10.30 and we'll resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll continue because I think I'm running out of time. I think I've been granted an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I want to stop discussing the brigade from Jablanica, but I have a document, a Defence document, 2D 00246. It's a Stojic Defence document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I'd just like to provide the Bench with some information. This document can be found in the bundle of documents that belong to my colleague Ms. Senka Nozica. So these documents concern the Stojic Defence. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see the document on the screen. Can you see the document on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document from the 44th Brigade from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it dated the 14th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble, they mention the responsibility of the Neretvica brigade, the problems in the municipality of Konjic and the zone of the Neretvica brigade.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that Hakalovic's brigade?
