utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: That's on the right bank of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now you mentioned an order. Your commander said I hereby order. Let's deal with Konjic first of all. Have a look at item 3 of this order issued by your commander. I'll try and read it through. Item 3: "The 2nd Battalion has the following task: Having completed mobilisation, use 1 Company to take up positions" --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see it on the screen? I can't follow it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see item 3?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Item 3 says, "The task of the 2nd battalion is as follows." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: "Upon completion of mobilisation, use the 1st Company to take up positions. The defence at the following line: Glodnica, Ostrozac." That's the last place in your municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Ostiste?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: That's a hamlet near Ostrozac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You know about the hamlet. "Be prepared to carry out an attack on the positions and units of the Croatian Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: "Use the 2nd Company, having completed mobilisation, to take up positions on Boksevica and be prepared to launch an attack." Is the Boksevica mountain a mountain that divides the municipalities of Jablanica and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Prozor, three municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Three municipalities. It includes Prozor. Very well. The 2nd Battalion of the 44th Brigade, when the brigade commander was carrying out Pasalic's order, did it say that they should participate with the Neretvica brigade under Hakalovic's command and that you should launch an attack? Have a look at item 3. It says, "Be prepared to carry out an attack on the positions and units of the HVO." Which is the -- in which place was the HVO present closest to Ostrozac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radesine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now that you have mentioned Radesine, tell the Court what happened in Radesine. Not on that day, but three or four days later?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps more than that but, yes, I know what happened there more or less. HVO members from Radesine blocked the Jablanica-Konjic road. They blocked the M-17 main road, and it wasn't possible to link up Jablanica and Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: What did your brigade do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our brigade didn't do anything. The -- our brigade wasn't involved in combat activity in Radesine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: And the ABiH from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The ABiH from Konjic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took Radesine and the population. Well, I don't know what they did to them but I know they attacked Radesine. They took the population somewhere and they captured or arrested the soldiers, but the 44th Brigade from Jablanica didn't participate in that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But you have provided us with some information. We will have a witness from the Spanish Battalion who will probably deal with that.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's no problem, but this is what I know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: In item 3, did the 44th Brigade use one of its battalion to cooperate with the Neretvica brigade and with Mr. Hakalovic, who was involved in action against the HVO in that area? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what it says? You want the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3, the 2nd Battalion task, is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we've read it out twice.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I put this? These are positions to the east of the municipality of Jablanica. There's the Recica mountain, Ostiste and Ostrozac. Globica is the neighbouring village beyond the lake. And apart from Radesine, there were no other units anywhere. They weren't really facing the HVO or, rather, this position wasn't much exposed to the HVO. It wasn't facing the HVO at that time. We had positions facing the Serbs on that axis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I don't want to say that you shouldn't make me laugh, it wouldn't be polite. I know where the positions facing the Serbs were, how far away they were. In Enes Kovacevic's order, on the second page, "The 3rd Battalion co-operates with the Neretvica brigade in the Konjic area in carrying out attack." That's what I asked you about. Did the brigade participate in the attack on the HVO in the area of the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander says, yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the municipality of Konjic, in the area of the Boksevica mountain, the brigade was involved in combat with the HVO but in the area of the municipality of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I'm not claiming that you entered deep into the rear of the Konjic municipality, but with Hakalovic and his brigade, the Neretvica, you pushed back the HVO in Kostajnica and that general area.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kostajnica, at this point in time, is at the foot of Boksevica. Now, the fighting at Boksevica lasted with lesser or greater intensity for a month.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that and we'll do that through a different witness, but I'd like to show you another document now compiled on the 24th of April. The number of the document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Just a follow-up question. The document as presented to you, sir, shows that the 2nd Battalion was supposed to take up offensive positions. Now, the preamble of this order indicates that the situation deteriorated, that there was general HVO movement and preparations going on designed to launch offensive operations against the BH army. So we see that the 44th Brigade is using all its effectives and you answered General Petkovic's question about that. Can you take a look at point 12 of that order, please. What does it say in point 12?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Points 12, it says: "Open fire only when given orders by the brigade commander and in case of an attack against the unit." THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the task was given on the basis of this order to the 1st Battalion, the 3rd Battalion, and the 4th battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of your recollections, was it the commander of the 44th Brigade that was supposed to give the final order for the troops to open fire? What happened with the 44th Brigade and your unit? How did you act?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this period, we were just trying to entrench and be prepared for an attack in the territory of the municipality. Nowhere were the units of the 44th Brigade outside their municipality, and nowhere did they launch into combat operations outside the municipality's territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this particular order, it has -- also has to do with the 2nd Battalion, which was engaged in an operation outside Jablanica. Now, my question is this: I can see point 10, where it is provided for the wounded and injured to be taken to the war hospital in Jablanica and the mobilisation of vehicles. So this is preparatory action that conforms to this order, but in point 12, it seems that the order must first be issued by the commander. But maybe there's some restrictions, and that's why I'd like to have your comments. It seems that there are two situations. One is that the commander has ultimately to give the order for the go-ahead, and in English it says "in case the unit is attacked." Now, how do you analyse point 12 in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but could you tell me the date of this document once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the 14th of April -- the 14th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. The 14th of April. That was the day when we were totally cut off, and we expected an all-out attack from all sides. And of course if somebody were to launch an attack, and the possibility existed in the Boksevica area for that to happen, and in Doljani, Sovici, et cetera. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I be allowed to continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to -- excuse me. I would like to add two questions here. One refers to what you have said, that you said that you prepared for an attack. Now, this can mean two things. It means that you prepared to carry out an attack or you prepared to be able to defend yourself against an attack from the other side. What was it that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to preparing for an attack against us. We had already been attacked in Ostrozac. In Ostrozac, on the 14th, there was a civilian fatality. That was a refugee from Foca. So we were already in combat and had to defend ourselves. We had to defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting in this military exchange --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: One more, please. Earlier on, during this military subject, the importance of military forces were mentioned with the result that there -- the ABiH largely outnumbered the HVO. Can you say anything about the firepower of these two bodies of troops? How would that compare? I believe it was a few hundred HVO or even less versus 2.000 ABiH. What was the firepower, the armament?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reverse proportionately. Our numerical strength was as it was and they were 10 times stronger technically, in technical terms. We didn't expect our local HVO to attack us. They didn't have the power to do so, nor were we afraid of an attack from our local HVO, nor were we afraid that the HVO from Jablanica would attack us. They didn't have the power to do so. But on the hills around Jablanica, a year before the war, heavy artillery weapons were positioned there and they were turned towards Jablanica, 155-millimetre cannons, 205-millimetre howitzers or 203-millimetre cannon at Risovac, mortars, tanks, and all the rest of it. Those are things that we could have just dreamt of. And we were afraid. We weren't afraid that we'd be attacked by the local HVO, but that the HVO from Western Herzegovina would attack us which came -- which did take place. The battalion from Siroki Brijeg attacked us, not the local HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And excuse me, Ms. Alaburic, if I have interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I interrupted you first, Your Honour, so I apologise to you. All I wanted to do was to follow on from a question that Judge Antonetti asked with respect to point 12 of this document. So, Mr. Idrizovic, would you clarify a point. Is it right to conclude that you could open fire in two cases? The first case is if an order is received from the brigade commander to open fire, and the second case would be when the unit is attacked, and then you would have to open fire in order to defend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, if the artillery were to win a war, nobody would need any infantry.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, General, but that artillery of yours killed 35 of our civilians, let alone the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: We're not going to talk in that manner, discuss things in that manner. We won't mention Livade, Doljani, and so on or anything else. Now document 4D 00140 is the next one that I'd like to take a look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have a calculation of the time used so far? THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, while we're waiting for the document, you said that the local HVO was not equal in force to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now you're going to see this unequitable position in the Konjic municipality for just a month. It is the 23rd of March, and this is the 24th of April now. So it's the space of a month. Let's see what happens. This is our department for refugees and displaced persons who sent out this document to all these international organisations.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you give us a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You have it on your screen. You have the document on the screen. It is a list of villages in Konjic municipality inhabited by Croatians of which some were burnt, looted, and Croats expelled. On the 23rd of March, you blocked Konjic, you arrested 150 Croatians, and this date is one month later on the basis of an unequal struggle. Do you know these villages, Trusina?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you not to take me to this area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened in Trusina on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The Prosecution has said a number of times and maintains its position, that whether the Muslims committed some crimes in some of these areas is not disputed, without going into any particular one at this point in time. That's why I'm always reluctant to get up and interrupt counsel or the accused when they're asking reasonable questions. But now, as the president already cautioned once today already, this is clearly offered for no purpose of no other reason then to take us down into a relevant area and tu quoque and into an area of the case that has nothing -- nothing is charged in Konjic. What -- what we've seen here this morning, I think Mr. Petkovic has shown us the military tactic of diversion. This is nothing to do with -- what happened in Sovici and Doljani has nothing to do with what happened in Konjic. Konjic is in the opposite direction. No one, neither the witness nor the Prosecution has ever suggested that the threat from the HVO came from Konjic. The threat from the HVO came from the north and to the west and this all -- all this about Konjic has taken up 45 minutes, an hour, and is completely irrelevant. I've not interrupted up until now. But now we go further and further into it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of General Petkovic is the last, not only in this courtroom, but generally who -- which would attempt to justify the crimes of one side by crimes committed on the other. I consider that to be untenable from the legal point of view and from the human point of view. The reason that we're showing this list of villages is not to attempt to justify the alleged crimes committed by the HVO with the alleged crimes committed by the BH army, it is a different reason. We're discussing, in fact, the ratio of forces, the balance of power between the HVO and the BH army. And I think that Judge Trechsel's questions were very rightly posed in that regard. But we do wish to prove that the BH army was far more powerful compared to the HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic, would you ask your questions then about this balance of forces and on the basis of this document. There are 23 villages, Croatian villages here. And we can see that the Croatians were expelled, that the villages were looted, burnt and so on. So ask your questions relevant to the document. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, from the 23rd of March and the blockade of the town of Konjic until the 24th of April, I showed you 24 villages taken over by the BH army in the Konjic municipality. Do you know about that or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, rumours were going round that certain crimes had been committed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: We're not talking about crimes here. Were the villages occupied?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you not to take me to other people's areas because then I would have to speculate, and I'm not here to do that. The time that we're discussing was far off, as far as we were concerned, and it didn't enter our minds to look at what was happening in Neretvica because we had too many of our own problems to contend with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, but I have another question. Was there a united system of command? The 4th Corps, two brigades in Konjic, one brigade in Jablanica. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that but it was a broader establishment as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking about that and was Esad Ramic and Tetak at any command post, forward command post there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: But the observation that can be made is that the 43rd, 44th and 45th Brigade was commanded by Arif Pasalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: And your TO Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I give the floor back to my Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, might I know how much time we've used up, so that I can organise myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have between 10 and 12 minutes, but the registrar will confirm that in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does that include half an hour from my learned friend Ibrisimovic, or is that just what's left of my hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. So it is with the half hour of -- with Mr. Ibrisimovic's half hour you have 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Idrizovic, I'd like us to discuss the moment, the events in Sovici and Doljani. And it has to do with a direct count in the indictment. Can you tell us, to start off, when the fighting began -- when the HVO engaged in combat in Sovici and Doljani. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 13th, we did not have effective communication with Sovici and Doljani. It was interrupted. All physical contacts were interrupted. So we didn't have any proper communication at all for me to be able to answer that question. We have seen a series of documents, and from the Tuta and Stela trials, it is common knowledge when that began. So you don't want me to speculate and do a lot of guesswork. It would be counter-productive.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you don't remember the exact date and that is quite understandable. Right. Now, you told us that the BH army units were in Sovici and in Doljani; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also told us -- that will suffice.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not sufficient. Let me say why, why they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday why they were established, and you also told us yesterday that the exclusive assignment of those units in Sovici and Doljani was in case of a conflict to evacuate the population towards Jablanica; is that right? That's what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: May we now take a look at the document -- document 2D 00246 once again, and I thank my learned friend Ms. Nozica for that document, and it is in the Bruno Stojic set of documents for the Bench. And I'd like to show point 5 to the witness, point 5 of that document. In point 5 of this order the commander -- from Commander Kovacevic it says as follows: "The 4th Battalion assignment immediately upon completion of mobilisation, the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Platoon should take up its positions towards Risovac, and the 5th Platoon in the village of Doljani and to be prepared for launching a defence, and until reinforcements arrive to reinforce the positions with one platoon and an armoured vehicle and not allow free passage in the direction of the villages of Sovici and Doljani." [Risovac]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Mr. Idrizovic, whether from what we've just read out of this portion from the 44th -- commander of the 44th Mountain Brigade it would emerge that the BH army in Sovici and Doljani did have a different assignment, not exclusively to evacuate the population towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Didn't have any other task in military terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, does this order show that there was some other task? I know you'll repeat what your position is, but just tell me: Does this order show what I have said?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this order before. This is the first time. I don't think it tallies with what I said earlier on. While I was the commander in command of the formation I have referred to, well, that was their exclusive task. Their task was that in the case of a Croatian attack the population should be evacuated. That's what these people in Doljani did, and the people in Sovici surrendered and what happened to them happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, this order depicts the situation differently from the way in which you depicted it when talking about the tasks of the ABiH in the villages of Sovici and Doljani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on. Yesterday you told us that the commander in Doljani prior to the attack, or just before the attack, if I'm quoting you correctly, managed to evacuate all the inhabitants in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: He managed to evacuate them all to Jablanica. You also said that some of the population of Sovici also managed to evacuate to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number. There were more people serving in the military rather than civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You don't consider people serving in the military as civilians?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those are -- who were serving in the army managed to break through to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say those serving in the army, you mean members of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. So the Sovici commander didn't accomplish his task to evacuate the population. Did he engage in combat with the HVO or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think there are a lot of documents about this, and in the Tuta and Stela case there were witnesses who have addressed the issue and there will also be such witnesses in this case, I believe, who will be in a better position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can I conclude that you had no information according to which the ABiH mounted resistance of some kind in Sovici? You don't know whether there was an armed conflict between two -- two armies?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there is an armed conflict people get killed. The HVO reports show that the action was carried out brilliantly without any losses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, we are discussing what you know. You are telling me that you don't know anything about this, and I just want to conclude with this issue saying that you don't know whether there was an armed conflict in Sovici or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents that I had and the documents that you have, and on the basis of the conversations with people up there, well, naturally, there was a conflict. People were attacked, and when they were attacked the commander surrendered and everything fell through.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did he surrender after having tried to resist or before? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what I heard from people up there, well, everyone saw things differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, at that time in Sovici were there 50 inhabitants of Prozor who were living in Sovici after the conflict in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you clarify something for us? Can you clarify part of your testimony when you said that in fact there were two conflicts and that the second conflict - and I'll quote to you - occurred after a member of Tuta's units had been killed, and after that event there were -- an even fiercer attack was launched. Can you tell us what you in fact wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You haven't quoted me correctly. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, then, can you clarify what you actually said.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that, it was within the context of an order from Mr. Petkovic or Praljak dated the 20th of February on the cessation of hostilities. I said that that order hadn't been implemented but that on the 24th - so not on the 22nd but on the 24th - a fierce attack was launched; this attack continued. I don't know whether you understand how war a waged. Probably not very well. But there was a fierce HVO attack on that day, on the 24th, and on that occasion Tuta's deputy was killed, and then revenge was taken in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's what I in fact want us to clarify. Before Tuta's deputy was killed, tell us what in fact happened in Sovici and Doljani. Had the military operation been completed within one day?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. How could it have been completed in a day? It continued for one year. The fighting continued for one year.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to understand your answers correctly, when you mention Sovici and Doljani, are you talking about what you know now in 2006; or are you answering these questions on the basis of the knowledge that you had when you were in Jablanica in April 1993; or are you telling us about this because you testified in the Tuta and Stela case and you learned about many things there? What I would like to know is when you answer a question in what capacity are you answering the question? Are you answering the question in the capacity of a former commander in Jablanica; or are you answering the question in your capacity as a witness in the Tuta and Stela case; or is it because in the meantime you have read a lot of material and you find yourselves -- you find yourself able to tell us a lot now? Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness answers Your Honour's question, could I just add I object to this current persistence in this line of questioning because counsel repeatedly says -- asks the witness questions about this. The witness repeatedly says, "I wasn't there. I don't -- don't ask me to speculate," and then turns around and continues to insist that he speculate, and can't have it both ways. He can either talk about Sovici and Doljani or he can't, but we're going in two directions at once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's because I noticed the problem that I would like the witness to tell me in what capacity he's answering certain questions, on what basis he's answering certain questions. Can you answer that question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. A minute ago I answered that question. I told counsel that there would be other witnesses appearing who could testify about Sovici. I wasn't there at the time, and I can't say anything about what I saw there because I didn't see anything there. What I know about that place is hearsay information or I read about it. So I told her that she should spoke to others about this, not to me. So you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm aware of the fact that the witness wasn't in Sovici or Doljani and that is why I put my question to him and asked him whether he had any direct information about the events in Sovici and Doljani. We have received his answer. As far as the objection raised by Mr. Scott, I'd like to draw your attention to part of the transcript, page 46 of yesterday's hearing. The witness said that after Tuta's deputy had been killed, his name was Cikota, he mentioned the date and he said after this member had been killed an even fiercer attack was launched and this was in order to take revenge. This was on page 46. The word "revenge" was repeated today, and I believe that it's my task to clarify what is at stake here, given the nature of these answers. And to clarify the word "revenge" I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that this is a term that is a key term with regard to the adjudicated facts from the Tuta-Stela case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Idrizovic, can you clarify the following for me. Yes, it's true that you referred to vengeance. On what basis? Did you read about this? Is this something you learned about in the Tuta and Stela case, or is it because in April you learned about this in Jablanica? So why did you spontaneously use the term "revenge"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found out about it in Jablanica very rapidly, because among the four men killed there was the brother of a member of the 44th Brigade command. Mustafa Skampo. There was an Skampo; he was the brother of an officer of ours. And the people who came from Sovici afterwards told us that this had happened, and this event was described by Rados in his diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, just for one second, Mr. President, because I'm getting a little agitated by the Prosecution standing up and saying that we're out of the scope. If you look at the proofing chart, he tells us the paragraphs of the indictment. Look at it very closely. He tells us that this witness is going to be testifying about certain paragraphs concerning Jablanica municipality, and he notes -- he notes paragraph 73, which is in -- which includes the area which counsel now is questioning on. And I think it's disingenuous for the Prosecution to stand up and saying we're going outside the scope. If the gentleman, if the gentleman doesn't know anything about those two incidents, then I -- I suggest that everything that the gentleman stated on direct examination be wiped off the record and not be considered. They can't have it both ways. On direct he can talk about it; on cross, when counsel go into it, we can't. We go by the proofing chart. The proofing chart states the paragraphs. They chose it. And so I think it's unfair for the Prosecution to stand up and to make these speeches interrupting counsel. It's highly unprofessional.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sorry, Your Honour, but I want to respond very specifically, because it's -- the questions -- first of all, in terms of the proofing chart, so-called, it referred to -- counsel just referred to paragraph 73 of the amended indictment, and I would -- I would ask the Chamber -- unfortunately I hate to take the time. But if you look specifically at the indictment, since this allegation -- a very specific allegation against the Prosecution has been made, if you look at paragraph 73 of the indictment, it is the introductory paragraph about the background of Sovici-Doljani and the make-up, the demographic make-up of the municipality, number one. Number two, in paragraph 76 of the amended indictment, it talks about the events on the 15th through the 17th of April, 1993. In the indictment at paragraph 76, it says the following: "A number of Bosnian Muslim men attempted to defend the villages of Sovici-Doljani, but most resistance was quickly overcome by late afternoon on 17 April 1993, when the Bosnian Muslim commander surrendered." That is the Prosecution case. It is not in dispute. We've never said anything to the contrary. There was a period of armed resistance early on the 17th of April. Our position is not to the contrary. Thirdly, the questions that were put to this witness about Sovici and Doljani yesterday were very specific as related to information that had specifically come to his attention; for example, when refugees and people who had escaped from the villages came into Jablanica and gave reports. So I object to Mr. Karnavas's characterisations and attack on the Prosecution. It's not fair or accurate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He asks the witness to provide hearsay information. The witness wasn't there. It was good enough for the Prosecution to ask for hearsay information. Granted, hearsay can come in in this Tribunal. Well, now we're trying to rebut some of the hearsay information and I think that's what counsel is trying to do. If they didn't want the gentleman to ask -- for the Defence to ask these questions, they could have avoided asking him for the hearsay information which he learned, because he wasn't an eyewitness. He wasn't there. And I think that we're entitled to -- under the rules of evidence to present alternative --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Alaburic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to explain why this question is being put. One of the counsel of the indictment, one of the items -- or, rather, one the paragraphs in the indictment concerns the torching of Muslim houses in Sovici and Doljani. The witness mentioned revenge being taken after Tuta's deputy had been killed, and as a result I think that it is in our interest to clarify this matter. I don't think that he spontaneously used the term "revenge," because whenever the witness referred to Cikota being killed he mentioned "revenge." But since I have not got enough time to clarify all these details, I'll ask the witness the following. Can we have a look at two documents that concern Sovici and Doljani. The first one is 4D 00447. It's a report from the 44th Mountain Brigade command which says that a commission composed of Sefer Halilovic, Milivoj Petkovic, and other ABiH representatives and HVO representatives arrived in the area. But what I'm most interested in is a sentence. It's the third paragraph in the middle of the page. "An unconditional evacuation of the civilian population from Doljani and Sovici has been agreed on and it will take place tomorrow." The word "an unconditional evacuation has been agreed on" is what interests me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were you present when ABiH representatives and HVO representatives held discussions in Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the number of the document, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D 00447. It's in the middle of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: There is no English translation, at least not in my file.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to ask my case manager about this who told me we had all the English translations. I do apologise. My case manager has told me that unfortunately this -- the translation of this document didn't reach us in time. This is why you don't have it. And in order to assist the Judges to see the sentence that I'm interested in, well, it's the 10th line on the screen, and it states the following: "An unconditional evacuation of the civilian population from Doljani and Sovici has been agreed on for tomorrow."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you see that sentence, Mr. Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: "Agreed" is the word I'm interested in. My question, and I'll repeat it, is: Were you present when Halilovic and Petkovic tried to agree on evacuating the population?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No. So you know absolutely nothing about that or do you have some information and, if so, what are your sources?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We can move on and have a look at the following document. I'd just like to draw your attention to one more thing. In this same document is the very next sentence as follows: "It was noted that the same commission made up of representatives of two armies and the international community moved in the direction of Konjic, set out in the direction of Konjic."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. We can move on. The next document is P 02203, and it is a letter sent by Paket post from Mostar signed by General Milivoj Petkovic, and it is a document in which the Greens are mentioned, Zeleni. I assume you are aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's about five buses coming to Sovici and Doljani to evacuate the population towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, the word "green" was used, and I'm going to ask you the following in that regard. Do you agree that this was sent on the 5th of May from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this Paket communication -- that it was sent to Doljani by Paket communication?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And do you agree, in Doljani, according to what it says in the upper right-hand corner, that it arrived on the 5th of May at 1130 hours?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it's not very legible but I take it that it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If from the report of the 44th Mountain Brigade of the BH army we saw that a delegation of the two armies, on that particular day, set out towards Konjic, would you agree with me that that same delegation or commission, on the 5th of May, was in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should have been. Mr. Petkovic is here. He knows whether they were there or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, tell me, with this possibility of communicating when General Petkovic was in Konjic, was it possible for him to send word to his service in Mostar to ask this about the buses, send this question to Doljani. Or rather, can a commander from Konjic tell his service in Mostar to send out a letter to an HVO unit in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? He has his deputy, the Chief of Staff, or whatever his name was who could do that in his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. And when somebody in Mostar compiles a letter with this wording, he writes the text independently, does he not? He words it independently?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In other words, this was written by somebody in Mostar in view of the fact that it was a letter sent from Mostar to Doljani; right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, since General Petkovic was in Konjic on that particular day, General Petkovic himself was not the author of the text and wording contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. That's pure speculation, Your Honour. We don't know if Mr. Petkovic dictated the exact language to someone in Mostar. We don't know if he did, but it's pure speculation to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm very pleased that my learned colleague Mr. Scott reacted because I think the burden of proof is on him and he can prove that General Petkovic from Fojnica dictated this kind of text this language.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Idrizovic -- yes, I'd like to give you some time to expand but I have very little time and I have more questions to ask you. With respect to calming down the situation, calming the conflict in Prozor, I'd like to comment some of your answers with respect to the exhibits presented to you by the Prosecutor. And I'll be as brief as possible, but let's start off with this. Take a look at document P 02088, please. It is a joint statement by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, who met in Zagreb on the 24th of April, 24th of April, in the presence of Lord David Owen and the Croatian representative of Franjo Tudjman and others. Tell us, please, Mr. Idrizovic, did you know that on the 24th of April, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic was in Zagreb talking to the Croatian representatives about mutual relations in an attempt to solve the problem of the conflicts and how to organise Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew about that, yes, because during the war in Jablanica, we had television. We could watch television. We had CNN. We had cable television. So we were able to watch different channels. We were not uninformed as we were in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, let us take a look at point 2 of this joint statement together. The end of point 2, in actual fact, where the following is stated: "That the signatories of this mutual statement, joint statement, order all military units of the BH army and HVO to cease-fire immediately and all hostilities in all locations where those military units are located and where they face each other." Have you -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, was Mr. Alija Izetbegovic in a way the Supreme Commander of the armed forces? I know that there was the collective Presidency.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he probably was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mate Boban was the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably he was. If he was the president, then according to the various documents, that would be so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at the end of point 3 of the joint statement where they take note, the highest representatives, if I can put it that way, of the Croatian and Muslim people in Bosnia-Herzegovina take note of the following: That the BH army and the HVO are equally legal units and the establishment of a Joint Command is indicated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now point 5 is the next one I'd like to take a look at. And at line 3 it says, "The signatories of this joint statement conclude that the responsibility for the conflicts are to be borne by both sides;" is that right? That both sides bear the responsibility -- are to blame for the conflicts; is that right? Is that what Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban say, that the BH army and the HVO have equal responsibility for the conflicts? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us take a look at another document, the number of which is P 02091. It is an addendum, annex to this joint statement, and it relates to the establishment of the commands of the BH army and HVO. And in point 1 of that annex it says, "That the BH army and the HVO will retain their separate identities and command establishment." Is that right, Mr. Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And point 2 says, "That they will establish or form a Joint Command which will be responsible for controlling the operations in military districts;" is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Now would you tell us the following: Do you know of the reactions in the BH army to this joint statement? What were they? And to this annex.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was talked about, and we firmly wanted to have a Joint Command for conflicts to cease, because to all intents and purposes at that time, we were waging war on two sides, and -- well, the conflict was completely nonsensical and led to the destruction, especially of us Muslims, because we were surrounded from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that the BH army, or at least the members of the BH army whom you knew, that they completely supported and endorsed these conclusions on the legality of the HVO and that the HVO was a component part of the armed forces of BH?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And there was a provision having the force of law stating who made up the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We did not receive any other kind of document to deny that, refute that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us take a look at three more orders on the cessation of hostilities which were compiled on the basis of this joint statement from President Izetbegovic and Boban. And I'd like to take a look at the following document, P 02084. It is an order by Mr. Bruno Stojic and Milivoj Petkovic on a cease-fire for all offensive operations towards the BH army. The date is the 25th of April, 1993, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And it was issued on the basis of the joint statement. It was a follow-up to that and an agreement on a cease-fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's see what happens next in the BH army. I had to select the documents, so I'm sorry for not showing them all to you but may we take a look at document 4D 00435 next, please, which is an order from the commander of the 4th Corps, Mr. Arif Pasalic, which once again relates to the previous joint agreement and orders a cessation to all offensive operations. Are you familiar with this document? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: May we now take a look at 4D 00436, which is another order by the commander of the 4th Corps, Arif Pasalic. And he warns and states in capital letters that a cease-fire take effect immediately. Have you seen this order before?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but probably, yes. If it was sent out to me, if I'm one of the addressees and the Municipal Staff is, then yes. I can't see the whole order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think it is my duty to draw your attention to the fact that here again we have no translation. So perhaps if we could be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really do apologise. We handed in these documents or many documents to the CLSS, and we also gave documents to a translation office in Zagreb, and we do some translations ourself as well for shorter documents which we need. So all I can do is apologise for those translations not being ready. If you consider it necessary, I can just say that my question referred to point 1. We can have that point translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You could read it. I understand your difficulties. I was not complaining, but I think in all honesty, you must know what we can read and what we cannot read. Otherwise, we cheat you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right, Your Honours. I do apologise. That's why I'm going to read out point 1 of this order, and we'll see what it says. It is an order from Mr. Arif Pasalic as commander of the 4th Corps in which he refers, among other things, to the previous order that we discussed, and point 1 is says: "I hereby most emphatically caution you that immediately," and that is written in capital letters, "unconditional and complete cease-fire be effected vis-a-vis the HVO units, and in case of provocation, act in the spirit of point 3 of the order," and the numbers follow, "of the 26th of April, 1993." Now, since the witness has said that he has probably seen this document before, my next question to him was this. A repetition of an order with these contents, does that mean that the BH army or, rather, the units of the 4th Corps did not abide by the order issued by their commanders of the 26th of April? Would that be the logical conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, nobody respected any orders, or this order, either side, when it came to cease-fire orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Idrizovic, I'd like to use the rest of our time to what we call the Prozor case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I'd like to hear your answer in full. You said that nobody respected orders. Why was that? Why was Pasalic's order not respected? That's what we're interested in hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these orders either on the HVO side or BH side were not put into practice. They were not adhered to in practice on the ground, not the ones before or the ones later. Now, it's difficult to -- for me to explain why. Quite simply, the fighting went on without cessation, we did receive orders, but nobody respected them on either side. Nobody carried out these orders. And this also says that or testifies the fact that Mr. Pasalic really did want to see a cease-fire, because he kept emphatically stating as much through these orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of any reactions against the non-compliance? Normally, in military service, non-obedience to an order is a rather serious offence. Were there any prosecutions of persons, lower commanders, who disregarded these orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no, on neither side. They were armies which were -- had been established just a little while ago and they were far from the kind of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a follow-up question. You have an order signed by Pasalic that was addressed to you which says "cease-fire". Now, let's take a hypothetical. One of your soldiers shoots at an HVO soldier. What did you do in such a case, or what would you do? Would you close your eyes to it, or would you arrest the soldier and send him up before a military tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking me, then my units, the units under my command, were a long way away from this. They were in town or around town. So this did not refer to where I was, and I don't know whether on either side one of the subordinate -- subordinates were held accountable for non-compliance with an order by his superior officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have an order of the 26th of April from Pasalic which says "cease-fire". Now, in your particular town, on the 27th of April, was there still shooting going on and, if there was, what did you as the responsible person do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not the responsible person at that time. It was my commander, the commander of the 44th Brigade in Jablanica who was responsible. He held the positions facing the HVO. I did not have any contact in that sense. My units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that others are still being blamed very often, but I'm talking about a hypothesis. The person who opens fire is under your command. You arrest such a soldier. Do you draft a report and forward it to the command of the 44th Brigade? Do you forward a report to Mr. Pasalic saying that in compliance with his order certain measures were taken against soldier X who opened fire? What would you say about that? Would you have taken any measures against such a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have taken measures against such a soldier if he'd been a member of mine. There were rules that were in force. A commander could take measures immediately, or he could send the individual concerned to the military prosecutor. But at the time, this judicial system hadn't been established. The state was in complete disarray. There was no efficient judicial system. There wasn't an efficient prosecutor's office. I'm not saying nothing existed, but it simply wasn't efficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I believe that the beginning of your answer provided to the question put to you by Judge Trechsel was very important, and I believe it will help the Judges and everyone else in the court to gain a better understanding of anything. With regard to measures taken for violation of orders, you said that both armies were in fact -- or had in fact only just been established, that they hadn't been fully established, and you have also said that the system was in a state of disarray, that the judiciary wasn't functioning during that period. So could you just finish the answer you had started giving, please? Or perhaps I should put a concrete question to you. Given that there were two newly-established armies, they had been in existence for perhaps about a year at that time, given that situation, did that reflect on the discipline? Did that influence discipline, the possibility of taking measures against soldiers when orders weren't carried out? Did it have an influence on the way in which the army functioned?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. General Petkovic, other professional soldiers know that you need several years to have an efficient brigade structure. Our brigades were formed on an ad hoc basis. The officers in those units weren't up to the tasks that they had to carry out. They weren't up to performing their duties that they should have been performing given their establishment rank. So the system was quite different. People often don't understand us when we discuss matters. We understand each other, but others don't. The situation was difficult. Let me just add this: Sovici and the commander over there often mentioned in this case, it wasn't possible to replace him though. We knew he was no good but if 80 per cent of the soldiers said if he's not the commander, then we won't remain members of the army. And there's no way if you're forcing someone to be a member of an army. How could you do that? There was no state in existence. Everything was done on the basis of patriotism. So the entire system was unstable. It's difficult to understand us when we talk about these things. It's difficult for the Judges to understand us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I believe that I understand you. I hope I understand you very well in fact. Now, could you answer the following: You described the situation that the ABiH was in, and I assume this was not only a situation that the ABiH was in. I believe the HVO was in a similar situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I move on to another subject, may I please be informed about the amount of time I still have at my disposal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar. You have already used up 111 minutes, and as you have 135 minutes, that means that you have another 24 minutes left. So you should conclude by half past 12.00 so that we can have the break. Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to know how we'll be working after the break, I retain my right to use the 15 minutes I have, and I know that my colleague from the Coric Defence has 15 minutes. I don't know what the position of Mr. Praljak is and I know Ms. Nozica has to conduct her cross-examination, so I'd like some instructions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, Mr. Ibrisimovic wants to keep 15 minutes of his time, which means that in theory, you have another 10 minutes. So you should conclude in 10 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, let's move on to the subject of Prozor. You have discussed this subject in detail, in greater detail than Jablanica, I would say. First of all, could you please have a look at the following document. Unfortunately, we don't have the translation, so we'll read out part of it. The number is 4D 00420. It's a daily report from Tactical Group 1 in Konjic. And on the 21st of October, 1992, it was forwarded to Sefer Halilovic. And I'd like to draw your attention to the date. It's the 21st of October. I'll summarise this report. Item 1 states the following: "Prozor has requested assistance in the form of units at the ready from neighbouring municipalities. The HVO has taken the Makljen hill, the border between Gornji Vakuf and Prozor. There is tension in the town, and the forces have been deployed in zones. Jablanica has sent in a company to the border of Prozor. All the other forces are at full combat readiness. "2. A company from Travnik which was on Igman is quite exhausted and has passed through here -- passed through here at 1900 hours. Instructions were given that they should go to Prozor." I'll skip the rest. "3. At about 1600 hours, Prozor reported that a Military Police Platoon and an armoured vehicle from Grude had been allowed to pass through Prozor. Their intention is to reach Travnik. An order was issued at 1620 hours to Gornji Vakuf that they should be stopped and returned to where they had come from. No report has been sent in response." I'll just mention item 4: "Roads from the south have been blocked for all traffic from Jablanica and from the south. The convoy of arms mentioned last night was stopped in Posusje. The total mobilisation was ordered in Konjic and the lining up of all armed persons in the barracks in Celebici was also ordered. Tomorrow we will be sending in two companies as reinforcement to Jablanica. The HVO units in Konjic are invisible." And that's sufficient for my question. On the basis of this document from the ABiH, can we conclude that individual army units were sent in the direction of Prozor on the 21st of October, 1992? Can we come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer that question with regard to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is this what the document shows?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak about Jablanica. I'll answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, let me just tell you something. I'm not asking you about what really happened. At this point in time, I would only like to analyse the document. So, please, tell me, was this something we can conclude on the basis of the document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the document, we can come to that conclusion. But this was never implemented. A company didn't leave for Jablanica and that's why the commander was replaced and I in fact replaced him. That's what I wanted to say. A unit wasn't sent in, but given the order, one could come to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, what you have just said is something that we will deal by referring to the relevant documents. Could we now have a look at the following document. We have a translation of this document. The number is 4D 00426. Again, it's from the commander of the Tactical Group in Konjic. It's a letter dated the 21st of October 1992, sent to Jablanica at 1330 hours, forwarded to the commander of the -- the commander of the Municipal Staff in Jablanica is asked to place all forces at his disposal in a state of full combat readiness and one unit is supposed to be sent in as assistance. Is that what you mentioned a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document 3D -- 4D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence would like to show that you sent troops to Prozor before the 24th of October. So, is the answer yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the answer is no. What does this document mean then? This document, dated 21st of October, 1330 hours, it was sent to Jablanica. So, to you, for certain. An this document states that you should send in a unit, that you should send a unit to Prozor. You didn't do this then. Have you seen this document or not? Did you receive this document or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, no, nothing was done. If I may explain this. This shows that the army was unstable. A Tactical Group 1, with its headquarters in Konjic, was intended to gather forces to raise the blockade of Sarajevo. That was its purpose and here it was becoming involved in something that wasn't really within the competence of command of the Tactical Group. Zejnil Delalic, he wasn't to be in command of the forces linked to Prozor or to other forces down there. But he got involved in that. We didn't act in accordance with this order. The staff didn't acted in accordance with this order and that's why the Staff Commander was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the document and we'll see why the municipal defence staff in Jablanica didn't act in accordance with this order. Let's have a look at document 4D 00419. Unfortunately, we don't have the translation of this document either, and so I would like to have a look at the second page of that document. I'll read out a small part of the document to clarify something for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just see if this document has a head and a tail, a title and a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You have this document in my bundle of documents. The number is 4D 00419.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will read out part of it. "Our unit couldn't carry out the task because of the concentration of the HVO forces, because of the level of fortification and because it's well-equipped. It would suffer great losses. And engaging the unit in this way would result in blocking the routes and would make it impossible to evacuate the wounded and killed, the wounded and refugees from Prozor. Engaging our units in the direction towards Prozor opens up the possibility for the HVO forces to carry out an attack on other axes in the direction of Risovac and Mostar." I'll skip the rest. Is this the explanation of the commander for the -- does this say why he didn't act in accordance with the order to send in a unit to Prozor?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said that the commander of the municipal defence staff in Jablanica was replaced as a result. Now let's have a look at document 4D 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could I just for understanding. What do we have to understand under the term of unit? It would be, in my experience, a company, some 150 or so people, but what did he -- did it signify here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something like a company, hundred to hundred fifty men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Document 4D 00418. We have the translation of this document. It's an order from the deputy chief of the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces. So we're talking about Sefer Halilovic's deputy, Mr. Jovan Divjak. The order was issued on the 25th of October, 1992. Item 1 says: "We hereby replace the command of the Municipal Defence Staff in Jablanica, Mr. Salko Zeren, because he failed to carry out an order to send unit to assist the Municipal Staff in Prozor. And this justifies -- he justified his failure to carry out the attack by referring to the order of the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command according to which action shouldn't be taken to contribute to worsening the conflict." Mr. Idrizovic, so this document shows the reasons for which the commander was replaced? THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I intervene? Item 1 states that Salko Zeren did not carry out the order, operative number one, of the deputy of the chief of the Main Staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on sending part of the unit to assist the municipal defence staff in Prozor. Who is the deputy chief of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jovan Divjak. It was Jovan Divjak in Konjic at the time. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague was saying something so I wasn't really following the question and answer, but I wanted to ask you a question about this orders on replacement. According to this order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be your last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've got such wonderful documents and I'm really sorry I won't manage to show them all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There will be other witnesses. There will be other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that it's difficult to cross-examine in this way, but I'll focus on one matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Jovo Divjak was detained because he had allegedly provoked the conflict between the Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know he was detained, but he wasn't the only one to encourage such conflicts. And there was a series of arrests. And I at least and others who worked with me are not clear about all of this. All those who are were arrested, imprisoned were released. And there is some speculation about that event. There was this attempt made in Parsovici in the Neretvica valley and the commander of the 45th Mountain Brigade, but what happened there, what they're trying to do, I really don't know. And I don't have any documents or I've never seen any documents about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In order to provide Mr. Idrizovic with relevant documents, could we have a look at 4D 00439?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that that was your last question. It's 12.30. We will now have our technical break, and I will ask the legal officer to calculate the time together with the registrar, the time remaining for the other Defence teams, in light of the time that has been granted by some Defence teams to others, and I'd also like to point out that General Petkovic's Defence has now completed its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mr. Scott wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I know time is precious, but I understand it's highly unlikely that we'll finish the witness today in any event unfortunately. And secondly, I'm also aware that at 1.45 we all tend to disappear sometimes quite quickly, so I didn't want to wait until the end -- end of the session. Just so that everyone is advised, and I'm not going to mention any witness names, because obviously we have a witness in the courtroom, tomorrow's first witness we'll be seeking protective measures concerning a pseudonym and facial image distortion. I won't go into the details now. I'm just putting everyone -- I'm just advising everyone that the witness will be seeking those protective measures. Secondly, Your Honour, the first witness on Monday, again, I'm not mentioning names, will be a 92 ter witness. I think that was previously disclosed but I just want to be -- I want to make sure. And also because of potentially tight schedule next week, the second week set -- sorry, the second witness set for next week, it's quite possible that we will be able to start that witness on Monday afternoon, on Monday and not Tuesday. Just so that people wouldn't be surprised, we may be able to start the second witness next week on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Scott. It's up to everybody to prepare then. I asked the legal officer and the registrar to make the calculations and on basis of that, Mr. Ibrisimovic has 15 minutes, the Defence of Mr. Coric will also have 15 minutes and Mr. Stojic's Defence has 15 minutes. No, I'm sorry, 30 minutes. And Mr. Praljak's Defence has 30 minutes as well. So three accused have 30 minutes and Mr. Ibrisimovic, representing Mr. Pusic, has 15 minutes. Those are the calculations. That would give us enough time to hear two more Defence counsel because we have 15 minutes for one and half an hour for another. That will take us up to quarter to 2.00. So go ahead, please. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think there has been some mistake because we had an initial 45 minutes of which we gave 10 minutes to the Prlic team which means that we have 35 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I know that you have a brilliant capacity to synthesize things, I'm sure you will be able to get through what you want in 30 minutes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Since the Judges always criticise us for not being coordinated as a Defence, during the break, we decided that I shall be starting off by showing a document to this witness that Counsel Alaburic didn't have time to show. It is 2D 00263, Mr. Stojic's document, and you have it in the Stojic bundle. Before it appears on e-court, let me tell you that it is a document from the BH army, the 4th Corps command. The document is dated the 25th of December, 1992, and we have the stamp of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the bottom to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command. In person it says, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, that is. And it is re your dispatch number such-and-such of the 23rd of December, 1992. May we take a look at page 2 so that we can see it is signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic. And I'm going to start off by reading the first paragraph, as soon as we get the second page on the screens. Can you see the signature, Witness, Mr. Arif Pasalic's signature.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right. We can go back to page 1 now and take it in order with paragraph 1. And it says the following, "On the 2nd of December, 1992, at 10.30 hours, members of the Neretvica Brigade, in a facility owned by Zejnil Delalic, Mr. Jovo Divjak was arrested. The reason that the above-mentioned measures were taken was that they were acting on the assumption that he was linked to individuals who on the territory of Konjic municipality had perpetrated a number of criminal acts and that Mr. Divjak had participated in issuing orders having, as their aim, the creation of hostilities and conflicts among the Muslim and Croatian people in the area." My only answer, and it stems from something that is obvious from this text, and you were asked this by my colleague before the break, whether you agree with me when I say that from this document it is clearly evident that Mr. Divjak was arrested and procedure taken because of creating conflicts between the Croatian and Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here but I can't confirm that because I think that you, too, have in your possession a series of documents signed by Mr. Divjak which speak to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
